StringWithMarkup.String: Safe Disposal of Pesticides. An empty pesticide container can be as hazardous as a full one because of residues left inside. Never reuse such a container. When empty, a pesticide container should be rinsed carefully three times and the rinsewater thoroughly drained back onto the sprayer or the container previously used to mix the pesticide. Use the rinsewater as a pesticide, following label directions. Replace the cap or closure securely. Dispose of the container according to label instructions. StringWithMarkup.String: /LABORATORY ANIMALS: Subchronic or Prechronic Exposure/ In a 90-day dermal toxicity study, male and female Fischer 344 rats (25/sex/group) were dermally exposed to 0, 0.5, 1 or 4 mL/kg/day STABILENE Fly Repellent (purity: polymeric, a.i. as measurement of a single component is not applicable). These dermal doses are equivalent to 500, 1000 or 4000 mg/kg/day. After 6-hour daily exposure, the dosing site was wiped with dry towel for the first 3 days. For the remainder of the study, the dosing site was wiped with damp towel. Systemic toxicity noted in the 4000 mg/kg/day group was statistically significant reduced body weight and reduced body weight gain throughout the treatment period. The differences in body weight were 8-11% for males and 3-6% for females throughout the treatment. At the 1-, 7-, and 13-week time points, the high dose male rats had a 66%, 28%, and 25% body weight gain decrement compared to control group and high dose females had a 53%, 19.8% and 19.5% body weight gain decrement compared to the control group. Body weight gains in the low and mid dose groups were not affected in either sex. There were no apparent effect on food consumption at any dose level tested, however, both sexes of the high dose group had reduced food efficiency for the first 7 weeks (25% for males and 18.6% for females) and the overall study (23.8% for males and 18.8% for females). The high dose (4000 mg/kg/day) females had a statistically significant increase in erythrocytes and decreases in mean corpuscular volume (MCV) at week 4. At week 13, high dose females had a statistically significant increase in erythrocytes, hemoglobin, hematocrit and decreases in mean corpuscular hemoglobin (MCH), MCV, and mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC). Dermal toxicity was noted in the mid and high dose groups as exfoliation (scaling) and/or excoriation (cracking) of the skin beginning at Day 7 for scaling and at Day 21 for cracking. The LOAEL for systemic toxicity was 4000 mg/kg/day based on reduced body weight gain, reduced food efficiency, and changes in hematological parameters. The NOAEL for systemic toxicity was 1000 mg/kg/day. The LOAEL for dermal toxicity was 1000 mg/kg/day and the NOAEL for dermal irritation was 500 mg/kg/day based on changes in the skin.

StringWithMarkup.String: /LABORATORY ANIMALS: Developmental or Reproductive Toxicity/ In a dermal developmental toxicity study, 25 presumed pregnant CD rats/groups were dermally exposed to 0, 0.4, 2 or 4 mL/kg/day of STABILENE Fly Repellent (purity: polymeric, a.i. as measurement of a single component is not applicable) from gestation days 6 through 15, inclusive. These dermal doses are equivalent to 400, 2000 or 4000 mg/kg/day. The dosing site was covered with 2 x 2-inch gauze and further occluded with a polyvinyl film attached to a specially designed jacket fitted with Velcro closures. Approximately 6 hours after daily application, the jacket and gauze were removed, the dosing site was wiped with a paper towel dampened with water, and blotted dry. Maternal systemic toxicity was noted in the mid dose group as reduced body weight gain decrement (45% and 15% reduction during gestation days 6-9 and 6-15, respectively). The high dose group had a 44%, 12%, and 15% body weight gain decrement compared to the control group during dosing period (gd 6-15), gestation period (gd 0-21), and dosing plus post dosing period (gd 6-21), respectively. In the high dose group, reduced body weight gain and an increase in total leukocytes and segmented neutrophils was observed. Maternal dermally related toxicity was noted as increased clinical signs of skin irritation in the mid and high dose groups during both the dosing period (gd 6-15) and the dosing plus post dosing period (gd 6-21). No developmental toxicity was noted at the dose levels tested. The LOAEL for maternal systemic toxicity was 2000 mg/kg/day based on reduced body weight gain and the NOAEL was 400 mg/kg/day. The LOAEL for maternal dermal toxicity was 2000 mg/kg/day based on increased clinical signs of skin irritation (exfoliation) and the NOAEL was 400 mg/kg/day. No developmental toxicity was noted at the highest dose tested (4000 mg/kg/day).
